name: Tax Alchemy
summary: Tax Alchemy offers strategic tax planning for business owners and real estate investors, with entity structuring, year-round advice, and flat-rate engagement pricing. Its public service model includes personalized advisory rather than education alone.
fit: Business owners or investors comparing a named tax strategy team, implementation responsibilities, and the complete cost of a planning engagement.
scenario: You have learned several strategies online but need to identify which fit your entity, income sources, and implementation capacity.
decision: Compare the actual advisory engagement rather than the size of the firm's educational audience. A course, a planning project, and a return-filing service have different deliverables. Request the assigned professionals and the timetable for completing each recommended action.
question: Which strategies, implementation tasks, and individual or business returns are included in the proposal?

name: Hall CPA
summary: Hall CPA, operating The Real Estate CPA website, markets tax planning for real estate investors, high-income earners, business owners, syndicators, and developers. Its public materials discuss entity structuring, depreciation, cost segregation, and real estate accounting.
fit: Rental owners and investors who need tax strategy connected to property operations, or sponsors with real estate partnership and reporting needs.
scenario: Your rental portfolio is growing while business distributions and household estimated taxes are becoming harder to coordinate.
decision: A syndicator's accounting needs can differ substantially from those of a physician buying a single rental. Compare the team's experience with your ownership structure and ask how business income, rental activity, and investor reporting will be coordinated.
question: Who coordinates the property study, partnership reporting, and the owner's personal tax return?

name: Keystone CPA
summary: Keystone CPA serves investors and business owners nationwide. Its homepage describes an initial review of income, businesses, entities, investments, and real estate, followed by a written tax plan with strategies and implementation steps.
fit: Investors and business owners seeking a written plan spanning their entities and real estate holdings.
scenario: You are considering another acquisition and want a decision framework before changing entity structure or ordering a study.
decision: Use the written plan to compare the two firms. Ask for deliverables, execution deadlines, and responsibility for filings rather than comparing lists of possible deductions. An investor with multiple entities should establish who coordinates the full return package.
question: Which implementation steps are performed by the firm, and which require the client or an outside professional?

name: Taxstra PLLC
summary: Taxstra is a Springfield, Illinois CPA firm serving clients nationwide. It lists strategic tax planning, tax preparation, bookkeeping, payroll, IRS representation, and specialized consulting for real estate investors, physicians, and business owners.
fit: Physicians, rental investors, and business owners seeking tax planning alongside preparation and ongoing accounting.
scenario: Your physician income, S corporation, and short-term rental have different reporting requirements but share one cash budget.
decision: A physician with 1099 income and rentals has overlapping decisions about compensation, estimated payments, retirement contributions, and property deductions. Compare a coordinated projection and the person responsible for each filing. Bookkeeping support may also matter when business records need cleanup before planning.
question: How will the team coordinate physician income, business compensation, and rental depreciation in one projection?

name: WCG CPAs
summary: WCG CPAs & Advisors lists small business advisory, S corporation elections, reasonable compensation, tax planning, accounting, payroll, rental property consulting, and multi-state tax work. The firm publishes fee ranges and describes customized service packages.
fit: S corporation owners and rental investors comparing ongoing accounting and tax planning packages.
scenario: Your S corporation is profitable, payroll is running, and you want to evaluate planning without disrupting filing deadlines.
decision: For an S corporation owner, compare the compensation model and payroll responsibilities as well as the return price. If rentals sit alongside the operating business, establish whether the package reviews both activities or only the business. Published packages still need a scope matched to your entity count.
question: Which owner-compensation analysis, payroll work, and real estate review are included in the selected package?

name: Tax Goddess
summary: Tax Goddess Business Services markets strategic tax coaching and tax strategy programs for business leaders, professionals, and entrepreneurs. Its homepage distinguishes programs for different business sizes and emphasizes clients with substantial annual tax bills.
fit: Profitable business owners comparing a strategy-focused engagement and the support required to implement it.
scenario: Your business has outgrown annual tax-season conversations and you want a more deliberate planning cadence.
decision: Evaluate the proposed strategies against your facts and the work required to execute them. A marketing savings example does not establish your own outcome. Ask for the planning assumptions, assigned professional, implementation calendar, and total fee before comparing the program with an AE engagement.
question: What specific actions, documentation, and filing responsibilities are included in the selected strategy program?

name: Prime Path Advisory
summary: Prime Path Advisory markets year-round tax strategy for founders, executives, and high-RSU earners making at least $1 million. Its public model describes strategy design, implementation, and filing with attorney and CPA coordination.
fit: High-income founders or executives comparing a private-client model with business and investment tax planning.
scenario: You have founder income and equity compensation and need to distinguish personal planning from company-level work.
decision: This is a closer comparison for an executive with substantial equity income than for a small rental owner. Ask which professionals review compensation, entities, and real estate together, and whether the quoted scope covers each return. Confirm the firm's income qualification before investing time in proposals.
question: How does the engagement coordinate RSUs and executive compensation with outside businesses or rental property?

name: Neil Jesani Advisors
summary: Neil Jesani Advisors presents three practices: mid-market advisory, private-client services, and tax controversy. Its public focus includes successful businesses and ultra-high-income individuals, with strategic planning, CFO services, and audit defense.
fit: Owners facing a liquidity event, private-client complexity, or tax controversy alongside planning needs.
scenario: You need a forward-looking plan while an existing tax matter requires a separate specialist or engagement.
decision: The firm's broader private-client and mid-market focus may be relevant when a business sale or complex dispute is driving the search. Compare specialist assignments and engagement boundaries. A rental investor seeking a limited depreciation project should first confirm that the firm's intake and scope fit that need.
question: Is the proposed work a tax project, CFO engagement, controversy matter, or a combination with separate fees?

name: Peter Holtz CPA
summary: Peter Holtz CPA combines timely accounting, proactive tax strategy, profit consulting, CFO advisory, and IRS representation. Its website states that clients generate at least $1 million in revenue and describes an integrated business financial advisory model.
fit: Established business owners comparing tax planning as part of a broader accounting and CFO relationship.
scenario: Your company shows accounting profit but cash available for taxes and distributions remains unpredictable.
decision: Compare reporting cadence, management advice, and the decisions your owner or finance team needs help making. An integrated CFO relationship may be useful when reliable financial information is missing. If the main issue is prior-year tax work or a rental purchase, ask for those deliverables explicitly.
question: What does the financial advisory relationship add beyond the tax plan and annual filings?

name: Rainwater CPA (James Rainwater CPA LLC)
summary: Rainwater CPA markets business tax advisory for seven- and eight-figure business owners. Its public service description includes quarterly projections, four planning meetings per year, tax preparation and filing, and tax resolution services.
fit: Established business owners seeking scheduled projections and planning connected with annual preparation.
scenario: You are happy with your preparer but want an additional review before the next year-end deadline.
decision: Compare a scheduled planning relationship with the specific work needed before a business decision. Ask how urgent events between meetings are handled and which records keep projections current. If rentals or depreciation changes are part of your situation, include them in the requested scope.
question: How are quarterly projections updated when a purchase, new entity, or major compensation change occurs?

name: P4 Tax
summary: Its public materials describe tax compliance, tax planning, and business structuring.
fit: Owners whose business structure and household tax position need to be reviewed together
scenario: You receive partnership income and operate a separate business, making the scope of a single quote difficult to interpret.
decision: Ask how K-1s, business structuring, personal planning, and compliance are priced and coordinated.
question: Which entities and owners are covered by the proposal?

name: Delerme CPA
summary: Its public materials describe accounting and tax advisory services for business owners.
fit: Entrepreneurs considering planning and accounting support with a defined service scope
scenario: Your business is changing markets or locations and you need to compare ongoing accounting support with a discrete tax-planning project.
decision: Ask which jurisdiction-specific work requires its own specialist and whether implementation and filings are included.
question: Who reviews the state and jurisdiction consequences before a move?

name: Anomaly CPA
summary: Anomaly CPA is a nationwide virtual firm serving startups, growing businesses, and real estate investors. Its listed services combine cloud accounting and monthly close with tax preparation and strategy involving QSBS, R&D credits, multi-state issues, and real estate planning.
fit: Growing businesses or investors that need proactive tax work together with accounting, reporting, or startup finance support.
scenario: You want a blueprint that can be followed by your bookkeeper, payroll provider, and return preparer.
decision: A venture-backed founder may need accrual accounting and diligence-ready financial statements in addition to personal tax advice. An owner-operated business may prioritize compensation and real estate planning instead. Compare the finance infrastructure you actually need with the tax work being purchased.
question: Does the quote include monthly close and investor reporting, or a separate tax strategy project?

name: Anderson Advisors
summary: Anderson Business Advisors lists tax planning, bookkeeping, entity formation and management, real estate asset protection, estate planning, and retirement services. Its public offerings include educational workshops and a Platinum membership alongside professional services.
fit: Business owners and investors comparing tax work with legal entity, estate, and asset-protection needs.
scenario: You need to decide whether a proposed ownership structure solves a legal concern, a tax concern, or both.
decision: Legal formation, membership access, and tax return preparation are different purchases. Compare each separately and identify the contracting provider for the work you need. If you need legal documents alongside tax planning, establish the attorney's role and how the tax and legal teams coordinate implementation.
question: Which work is covered by membership, and which requires a separate tax or legal engagement?

name: Gelt
summary: Gelt offers year-round tax strategy, compliance, and a tax management platform. It lists business and individual filing services and separately scoped strategy plans, with industry pages for healthcare, technology, professional services, and real estate investors.
fit: Business owners and investors who want planning and compliance coordinated through a tax management platform.
scenario: Your income has become more complex and you want to understand what the platform and assigned professionals each deliver.
decision: Compare the professional service delivered through the platform rather than the dashboard alone. Ask how projections are reviewed, which entities are covered, and how implementation is assigned. Where published compliance and strategy prices are separate, add them before comparing first-year cost.
question: Which strategy services are included beyond compliance, and which are separately scoped projects?

name: Jasmine DiLucci
summary: DiLucci CPA Firm lists tax planning and preparation, bookkeeping, and IRS tax resolution. Its site identifies Jasmine DiLucci as an attorney, CPA, and enrolled agent and presents services for business tax and accounting needs.
fit: Business owners comparing tax planning with bookkeeping or an existing IRS resolution need.
scenario: You have a tax notice and also want to improve next year's planning once the current issue is understood.
decision: If an IRS notice or collection issue is driving the search, compare the professional assigned to that case and the representation scope. Future planning and historical resolution may require different projects. An owner with rentals should also identify who reviews depreciation and coordinates the related returns.
question: Will the same engagement cover the IRS matter, ongoing books, and forward-looking planning?

name: Creative Planning
summary: Its public materials describe wealth management with tax, estate, and related planning services.
fit: Households seeking coordination between investment management and tax planning
scenario: You already have an investment adviser and want to decide whether tax work should sit inside that relationship or alongside it.
decision: Ask whether tax planning can be evaluated separately from investment management and estate services.
question: What fees and deliverables apply to the tax work itself?

name: Range.com
summary: Its public materials describe wealth management integrating tax, investment, retirement, and estate planning across service tiers.
fit: High earners who value a connected financial platform and ongoing advice
scenario: You want a consolidated financial view but your immediate priority is a specific tax decision involving income or a business.
decision: Ask which membership tier includes proactive tax planning and filing and what happens at renewal.
question: Does my selected tier include the tax work I actually need?

name: Dark Horse CPAs
summary: Dark Horse CPAs markets tax advisory and compliance, accounting, and business financial support. Its public tax materials describe planning with a CPA and expertise including rental properties, stock compensation, 1031 exchanges, and multi-state filings.
fit: Business owners seeking a CPA relationship that combines tax planning with accounting or broader financial guidance.
scenario: Your business reporting needs and personal planning needs are expanding at the same time.
decision: A broad firm can offer many specialties, but your assigned professional and engagement scope determine the service you receive. Compare the actual CPA's experience with your business and rentals, the reporting schedule, and how projections feed management decisions. Ask for a distinct price for accounting, advisory, and return preparation.
question: Which CPA will own the relationship, and what planning, accounting, and CFO work will that person deliver?

name: Cerebral Tax Advisors
summary: Cerebral Tax Advisors specializes in medical professionals and private practice physicians. Its public model emphasizes tax plan implementation, filing, and verification, including situations combining W-2 income, independent-contractor business income, and real estate.
fit: Physicians and healthcare practice owners seeking implementation support across medical income and investments.
scenario: You own a practice, receive professional income, and hold rental property outside the operating entity.
decision: A locum physician, a hospital employee with rentals, and a practice owner have different planning and accounting needs. Compare the package applicable to your profile, the professional access provided, and which filings are covered. If evaluating a savings guarantee, read its eligibility conditions and exclusions.
question: Which medical-income and investment activities qualify for the selected package, and what execution work is included?

name: The Tara CPA Firm
summary: The firm markets ongoing planning, federal and state preparation, quarterly estimates and strategy calls for profitable entrepreneurs.
fit: Owners seeking proactive tax support as profit grows
scenario: A consultant has growing profit, irregular owner draws and a spouse with employment income. Last year's estimates no longer reflect the household. The next decision is how to update the projection before another large client payment arrives.
decision: Request an estimate-review engagement first if your current preparer already has accurate records. A broader planning relationship becomes more useful when income changes repeatedly require decisions throughout the year.
question: How will the plan change when my business outperforms its forecast?
note: A regular meeting is useful only if the numbers feeding it are current. Determine who updates the projection after a significant income change and how the owner learns that a payment needs attention.
documents: Current profit and loss and open receivables; Owner draws and payroll year to date; Spouse withholding and outside income
deliverable: a dated household projection with an income-change trigger and next payment instructions

name: Fraim, Cawley & Company CPAs
summary: Its practice lists tax preparation, advisory, bookkeeping, business valuation, forensic accounting and exit planning.
fit: Owners seeking help with operating decisions or a business transition
scenario: An owner has received an unsolicited acquisition inquiry but has never reconciled personal expenses, related-party rent and discretionary compensation. The immediate job is preparing a consistent earnings picture before discussing a purchase price.
decision: Keep the existing preparer for open returns while commissioning a defined exit-readiness project. If valuation or forensic work is required, compare providers qualified for that specific assignment before selecting the owner tax planner.
question: Who coordinates the operating plan with a possible future sale?
note: Valuation, deal negotiation and tax modeling are different assignments. An exit proposal should identify who prepares the earnings adjustments and who reviews transaction assumptions with legal counsel.
documents: Three years of returns and financial statements; Related-party leases and compensation history; Draft buyer inquiry or proposed terms
deliverable: an agreed earnings reconciliation and a separate transaction-review timetable

name: Wellness Fi
summary: Wellness Fi lists quarterly or monthly bookkeeping, practice advisory, estimates and tax strategy. Annual filing can be added; its published scope treats other businesses, property and cleanup as additional work.
fit: Therapists and mental-health practice owners seeking industry-specific operational support
scenario: A therapist sees steady patient demand but is unsure whether monthly accounting is needed. A second revenue stream and a rental property have also appeared. The decision is which recurring practice services to buy and which outside activities need their own scope.
decision: A specialist planning engagement can complement the practice bookkeeper. Compare a full migration only after the proposed replacement explains how clinical receipts, business records and household information will be reconciled.
question: Will adding clinicians change the scope or price of the engagement?
note: A practice bundle can be a good fit without covering every household activity. Quote the practice work separately from the new business and property so the owner can see which records and fees belong to each.
documents: Practice revenue and expense history; New revenue-stream agreements; Property income and depreciation schedules
deliverable: a reporting-cadence recommendation and separate scope for each income source

name: Taxhub
summary: The US Taxhub site lists tax preparation, consultation, bookkeeping, S-corporation conversion and Form 5472 filing. This comparison concerns gettaxhub.com, not similarly named overseas providers.
fit: Taxpayers who primarily need a return prepared through a remote service
scenario: An independent professional needs a business return prepared and wants to discuss a possible entity change. The owner also receives a partnership K-1. The practical question is whether one proposal covers preparation, the decision analysis and the subsequent implementation.
decision: If preparation works well, keep it and add a decision-specific consultation. If several entities and personal investments need coordinated review, request a planning proposal that names all of them rather than adding isolated calls one at a time.
question: Does the quote cover next year's decisions or only this year's return?
note: An available consultation does not automatically establish the deliverables of an entity project. Obtain the analysis, filing assignments and ongoing payroll responsibilities before treating a conversion as completed.
documents: Current entity documents and prior elections; Business ledger and year-to-date profit; Partnership K-1 and distribution history
deliverable: a preparation scope plus a separate entity-decision work plan

name: Collective
summary: Collective markets a subscription back office for self-employed owners, including bookkeeping and tax support. Its S-corporation offering includes entity-return and payroll-related services; confirm partner roles and personal-return coverage in the selected plan.
fit: Solo owners evaluating business setup, bookkeeping, payroll, and tax support together
scenario: A solo designer wants less administration but has just added a second business and purchased a rental. The question is whether the existing subscription still fits the owner's complete situation or whether a separate planning relationship is needed.
decision: Retain a convenient back office while commissioning coordinated owner planning if the services can exchange complete records. A full replacement should explain how bookkeeping, payroll, return preparation and decision review continue without gaps.
question: What happens if I add a rental or a second business?
note: Convenience within one workflow can conceal work outside it. Make a list of every return and decision before assuming one monthly charge covers the second activity, rental records and household planning.
documents: Entity list and ownership percentages; Payroll setup and recent reports; Rental acquisition and depreciation records
deliverable: an entity-by-entity coverage map and an exportable implementation record

name: Xendoo
summary: Xendoo publishes online bookkeeping, catch-up work, financial reporting and CPA-delivered tax planning and filing, alongside dashboard-based financial insights.
fit: Small businesses whose first priority is reliable books and recurring financial visibility
scenario: An online seller has deposits from several channels but cannot reconcile refunds, processor fees and transfers. Tax planning has stalled because reported profit changes every time the ledger is reviewed. Reliable books are the first dependency.
decision: Commission bookkeeping cleanup before changing the tax advisor if record quality is the bottleneck. When comparing bundled providers, ask to see the proposed reconciliation process and the first month in which planning can use accepted numbers.
question: When will my financial records be ready for a planning review?
note: A tax recommendation based on unreconciled payouts may need revision. Define the cleanup completion standard before using the ledger to project income or approve owner distributions.
documents: Marketplace and payment-processor reports; Bank and credit-card statements; Prior ledger and filed business returns
deliverable: a reconciled opening balance and a documented books-to-tax handoff

name: Pilot
summary: Pilot publishes business tax preparation and filing alongside bookkeeping and broader financial-management services. Pilot.com is distinct from the CPA Pilot software already covered elsewhere on this site.
fit: Startups seeking company-level compliance and a scalable accounting relationship
scenario: A founder is moving from initial bookkeeping to investor reporting. Corporate deadlines, employee payments and the founder's personal investments are now being discussed together. The owner needs to know where the company engagement ends and personal advice begins.
decision: Keep startup accounting if it meets reporting needs and add a founder tax planner for outside activities. Compare a replacement only when it can explain the corporate calendar and preserve the reporting investors already rely on.
question: Does company tax support include my personal founder tax decisions?
note: A company finance workflow and a founder's household return can have different responsible professionals. Separate corporate compliance, management reporting and owner planning before evaluating the total quote.
documents: Corporate formation and ownership documents; Current financial statements and payroll; Investor-reporting requirements and owner income
deliverable: a corporate compliance calendar with a separate founder-planning assignment

name: Decimal
summary: Decimal lists federal and state preparation, planning, estimates and entity guidance for small and midsize businesses. Its tax service materials discuss working with clean books, including records maintained elsewhere.
fit: Owners seeking a recurring operating-accounting relationship
scenario: A home-services owner likes the current bookkeeper but wants a more deliberate tax process. Seasonal income and equipment purchases make last year's payments a poor planning reference. Replacing the ledger provider may be unnecessary.
decision: Compare tax-only or planning-only proposals before buying a bundled accounting replacement. If record delays repeatedly prevent review, include a monthly close service in the shortlist and specify the date the tax team receives usable reports.
question: Can my existing accounting workflow support a separate written tax plan?
note: A new advisor needs an accepted data cutoff and a correction process. Specify who resolves coding questions and how later ledger adjustments affect a projection that has already been delivered.
documents: Monthly financial statements and general ledger; Equipment purchase and financing records; Prior estimates and payment confirmations
deliverable: a books-acceptance checklist and seasonal estimate update schedule

name: Fondo
summary: Fondo markets startup bookkeeping, tax filing and tax-credit work. TaxPass describes corporate federal and state returns, Delaware franchise-tax work and separately scoped international additions.
fit: Startup founders seeking organized company compliance and accounting support
scenario: A small startup has raised capital and the founder has heard about stock-related tax planning. Corporate filings still need completion. The first task is collecting ownership and issuance records rather than treating a questionnaire result as a personal tax conclusion.
decision: Pair a functioning corporate tax service with a specialist owner engagement if responsibilities can be defined cleanly. An alternative should identify the exact stock records it needs and avoid promising a result before reviewing them.
question: Which work relates to the corporation and which relates to me personally?
note: A screening tool cannot replace review of actual ownership history. Ask who performs founder-level analysis, what assumptions are tested and whether that work is separate from corporate filing.
documents: Stock issuance and capitalization records; Corporate returns and financial statements; Foreign ownership or transaction documents
deliverable: a corporate filing calendar and a separately documented founder-record review

name: Kruze Consulting
summary: Kruze markets tax services for venture-backed startups, with accounting and financial-support work positioned around funding and growth stages.
fit: VC-funded companies seeking finance support aligned with startup operations
scenario: A founder's company needs finance support for a funding round while the founder is buying an investment property. These are simultaneous decisions with different evidence and stakeholders. A proposal should separate company reporting from personal acquisition planning.
decision: Maintain startup finance support when it serves the board and commission owner planning separately. If seeking a single replacement, require evidence that it can meet investor reporting requirements as well as the owner's individual assignment.
question: Who handles the founder's planning while the company prepares for financing?
note: Investor-facing company work should not be displaced simply because the founder's personal tax needs changed. Clarify who receives business information and which professional coordinates household decisions.
documents: Funding documents and investor reporting calendar; Corporate financials and payroll; Property purchase documents and personal returns
deliverable: separate corporate and owner workstreams with a named coordination contact

name: Heard
summary: Heard markets a financial platform and professional support for therapists, including bookkeeping, estimates and plan-dependent annual filing. Payroll and some tax services depend on the chosen plan or add-ons.
fit: Therapists evaluating an industry-focused accounting service
scenario: A solo therapist is preparing to hire clinicians and move from a simple practice to a group. The owner must decide whether a plan upgrade covers new payroll and business-return responsibilities or whether additional advisory work is required.
decision: Compare a plan upgrade with a practice-focused accounting engagement before migrating. Add owner planning separately when outside businesses or property create questions beyond the practice workflow, and confirm data access in either arrangement.
question: Which changes in my practice require an updated engagement?
note: Plan names do not establish identical tax coverage. Compare the actual business return, personal return, payroll and support entitlements of the proposal that applies after the first hire.
documents: Practice entity status and previous returns; Hiring timetable and compensation proposals; Current books and platform export options
deliverable: a first-hire responsibility checklist and a complete first-year service quote

name: Acuity
summary: Acuity publishes bookkeeping, accounting, tax and CFO services with configurable support by business stage. Current site materials identify Acuity as powered by Sorren; confirm the contracting entity and professional responsibilities.
fit: Businesses needing a dependable finance operation and advisory reporting
scenario: An ecommerce brand has outgrown owner-managed books and needs inventory reporting, sales-channel reconciliation and income-tax work. The owner also wants personal planning. One engagement may handle operations while another handles the household.
decision: Compare an accounting upgrade with a full-service replacement. If the accounting team already delivers reliable reports, use those reports for a separate owner-planning engagement rather than duplicating the monthly close.
question: Who translates monthly reports into a transaction planning model?
note: Sales-tax compliance, inventory accounting and income-tax planning use related records but remain separate responsibilities. Ask each proposal to assign these workstreams and name the professional reviewing owner-level decisions.
documents: Inventory movement and cost records; Channel settlements and sales-tax registrations; Entity returns and owner income records
deliverable: a staged accounting roadmap with separate tax and owner-planning assignments

name: Tax Hack Accounting Group
summary: Tax Hack describes tax advisory and compliance for internet, software and ecommerce businesses, with a portal and recurring planning meetings.
fit: Online businesses that need advice tied to their operating model
scenario: A software owner has contractors in several places and is increasing development spending. The owner wants to understand which activities require specialized review and how recurring planning connects with return preparation.
decision: Add a defined technical review if the current tax process works but a new project requires more evidence. Compare recurring advisory providers when decisions arise frequently and the same records must be updated throughout the year.
question: Which platform and jurisdiction records do you need before advising me?
note: An industry label is useful context but does not define the evidence needed for a specific project. Require the provider to identify missing records, any specialist work and the implementation deadline before relying on projected benefits.
documents: Contractor agreements and payment history; Development project and expense records; Business returns and operating-state list
deliverable: a record-request matrix and an agreed specialist-review sequence

name: JETRO and Associates
summary: JETRO's fitness site publishes remote bookkeeping, year-round tax planning, annual preparation and payroll for gym and studio owners.
fit: Gym and fitness owners seeking industry-specific operational support
scenario: A first-location gym owner has trainers, membership receipts and payroll deadlines but no reliable monthly reporting. The owner wants an advisor who can help establish routine records before discussing a property purchase.
decision: Compare a gym-focused bookkeeping and payroll service with adding tax planning to existing operations. Where a property decision is the new requirement, a separately scoped planner may complement the fitness back office without moving payroll.
question: How will a second location change the planning and accounting scope?
note: Recurring payroll and membership administration cannot pause during a tax-advisor change. A transition proposal should preserve employee payments and define which closing month becomes the new team's responsibility.
documents: Membership-system settlement reports; Payroll registers and contractor records; Studio lease and monthly expenses
deliverable: a first monthly close calendar and an uninterrupted payroll handoff

name: Vincere Tax
summary: Vincere lists tax preparation, planning, consulting, representation and bookkeeping. It also advertises white-label tax services for financial-planning practices.
fit: Owners who want tax work connected with their broader financial advisers
scenario: An owner already uses a financial planner and wants business tax work integrated with that relationship. A liquidity event is approaching. The owner needs to know who makes the tax recommendation, who communicates it and who implements the agreed action.
decision: Compare a planner-coordinated tax relationship with hiring an independent tax advisor who collaborates with the planner. Require the same records, consent process and decision timetable so branding does not obscure responsibility.
question: Will my adviser receive an actionable summary of the tax implications?
note: A familiar advisory brand can front a different tax-service provider. The engagement should identify the tax professional, permissions for information sharing and the party responsible for direct client follow-up.
documents: Current financial-planning assumptions; Business ownership and transaction documents; Consent and existing advisory agreements
deliverable: a communication map naming the tax reviewer and implementation owners

name: Little Fish Accounting
summary: Little Fish publishes accounting, tax support and advisory for service-based businesses with small teams, with ongoing bookkeeping positioned as part of its service model.
fit: Service providers who want organized books and tax support
scenario: An agency owner is deciding whether to add a team member or keep the company deliberately small. The owner needs accurate profit and a household tax projection before choosing a sustainable compensation target.
decision: Compare ongoing advisory accounting with a narrower tax-planning engagement if the records are already dependable. The proposal should respond to the owner's goals, including a deliberate choice to limit growth, rather than assuming expansion is always the objective.
question: What reporting will be available before the next planning decision?
note: Revenue growth does not automatically improve owner cash availability. Ask the advisor to distinguish a hiring forecast, the company's reported profit and the household payment estimate rather than using one number for all three.
documents: Client revenue and capacity assumptions; Proposed employee cost and payroll timing; Owner income targets and current estimates
deliverable: a staffing decision brief tied to separate business and household forecasts

name: The Bottom Line CPA
summary: The Bottom Line CPA markets financial and tax services with a Profit First emphasis, a dedicated profit-and-tax team and secure client communication.
fit: Online sellers seeking accounting that reflects inventory, platforms, and cash allocation
scenario: A profitable owner uses separate cash accounts but still receives unexpected tax-payment instructions. The next question is whether allocation percentages are being reconciled with a current projection and the owner's outside income.
decision: Keep a useful cash-allocation system while requesting a documented projection review. Compare broader advisory relationships if the owner also needs recurring interpretation of profit, compensation and available cash before making decisions.
question: Which cash-flow reports will support the tax forecast?
note: Cash set aside is a funding decision; projected liability is an analysis based on records. Ask how the two are reconciled when profit, payroll or household income changes rather than assuming the bank balance proves adequate preparation.
documents: Cash-account balances and transfer history; Business profit and owner payroll; Outside income and estimated payments
deliverable: a reserve-to-projection reconciliation with clear update triggers

name: The Fitness CPA
summary: The Fitness CPA markets accounting, taxes, payroll and financial operations for fitness businesses, with franchise and expansion-related advisory materials.
fit: Gym owners evaluating financial guidance with industry context
scenario: A studio owner is evaluating a second location and new equipment financing. The tax advisor needs to coordinate the opening budget, staffing plan and owner cash requirements before any forecast is treated as a green light to expand.
decision: Compare fitness-focused operational advisory with adding an owner tax planner to the existing team. A replacement should preserve location-level reports and explain the evidence needed before supporting an expansion decision.
question: Who reviews the facility acquisition separately from operating results?
note: A location forecast and an owner tax plan serve different decisions. Compare who reviews lease commitments, cash runway and tax timing, and specify whether financing assumptions are tested or merely accepted from the owner.
documents: Proposed lease and opening budget; Equipment financing and staffing proposals; First-location reports and owner income needs
deliverable: an expansion-readiness work plan with a separate owner payment projection

name: Accountfully
summary: Accountfully publishes bookkeeping, accounting, tax planning and filing for businesses, including consumer brands. BELAY acquired Accountfully in 2025; verify the current service brand and contracting arrangements.
fit: CPG brands needing reporting that reflects inventory and distributor economics
scenario: A small packaged-goods brand is growing wholesale orders while inventory absorbs cash. The owner wants tax planning but also needs reliable product margins and lender-ready records. These assignments should be priced and scheduled separately.
decision: Compare an inventory-capable accounting provider with retaining the ledger team and adding owner tax planning. Confirm how the current service organization handles access, continuity and responsibilities before migrating records.
question: Will the year-end numbers reflect inventory and distributor adjustments?
note: A business can report earnings while struggling to fund inventory. Ask the provider to separate inventory accounting, operating cash forecasting and tax projections so each decision uses the right report.
documents: Inventory counts and purchase commitments; Wholesale contracts and receivables; Lender requirements and prior returns
deliverable: an inventory-close schedule with separate lender and tax reporting outputs

name: Blumer CPAs
summary: Blumer lists accounting, tax, payroll and advisory for entrepreneurs, with service-business and creative-agency positioning and growth-related consulting.
fit: Creative firm owners seeking finance support tied to their growth model
scenario: A creative agency has profitable projects but uneven capacity and partner compensation. The owners want to change the delivery model before year-end. Tax planning needs to work from the revised business assumptions rather than last year's structure.
decision: Compare agency advisory accounting with a decision-specific tax engagement. If the business model still needs work, resolve those assumptions first; a tax projection based on an unapproved staffing plan can create false confidence.
question: Will the forecast incorporate my revised agency growth plan?
note: Business-model consulting and tax implementation may require different deliverables. Specify who updates the staffing and margin assumptions and who turns the approved operating model into a tax-review brief.
documents: Project margin and capacity reports; Partner agreements and compensation history; Proposed delivery-model and staffing changes
deliverable: an approved operating-assumption set and a linked tax-action schedule

name: Fusion CPA
summary: Fusion lists tax planning and filing, accounting cleanup, controller and CFO support, and accounting-software services including QuickBooks and NetSuite work.
fit: Owners needing business accounting and tax coordination across entities or jurisdictions
scenario: A family business is moving to a new accounting system while owners discuss distributions and a related-party property transaction. Tax work needs stable balances and a defined point at which migrated records can be used.
decision: Compare a software-capable accounting provider with keeping the implementation consultant and hiring a tax planner. The handoff should identify accepted balances, unresolved issues and the date planning can begin using the new system.
question: Which jurisdictions and entities are specifically listed in the engagement?
note: Software migration can change account mappings without changing underlying economics. Ask who validates opening balances and which version of the ledger supports the planning analysis before approving distributions.
documents: Old ledger export and migration mapping; Owner distribution and loan schedules; Related-party agreements and property records
deliverable: a validated opening-balance package and a separate owner-decision timetable

name: GreenGrowth CPAs
summary: GreenGrowth advertises tax, accounting, audit and CFO advisory across industries with complex reporting requirements, including cannabis, technology and real estate.
fit: Businesses seeking finance support in sectors with added reporting complexity
scenario: A regulated business needs a lender-requested financial report while its owner seeks personal tax planning. The first step is determining the exact assurance requirement and the qualifications needed for that engagement.
decision: Choose an appropriately qualified assurance provider when that is the actual requirement. AE can be evaluated for a separate owner-planning engagement; it should not be treated as a substitute for external assurance or industry-specific compliance responsibilities.
question: What work needs industry-specific expertise beyond a general tax plan?
note: A tax-planning proposal cannot substitute for a specified assurance engagement. Obtain the lender's written requirement and identify independence and reporting obligations before selecting the firm responsible for that work.
documents: Lender reporting request and loan agreement; Regulatory obligations and entity records; Financial statements and owner returns
deliverable: a confirmed reporting specification and a separate owner-planning scope

name: SDO CPA
summary: SDO CPA publishes year-round planning and compliance for business entities, including multi-entity and intercompany considerations and property-related coordination.
fit: Owners evaluating compliance and entity-related planning support
scenario: Two partners operate a service company and a separate property entity. Intercompany transfers and owner contributions have been recorded inconsistently. Before discussing strategy, each entity's balances and ownership records need to agree.
decision: Compare a multi-entity planning engagement with a targeted reconciliation project if records are the main problem. If multiple preparers remain involved, require an agreed K-1 delivery schedule and a single record of unresolved issues.
question: What changes operationally if the recommended entity election is made?
note: A consolidated owner view can hide discrepancies between legal entities. Require a reconciliation of transfers, loans and contributions before treating cash movement as taxable income or available distribution cash.
documents: Entity ownership and governing agreements; Intercompany and owner transaction ledgers; Property leases and prior K-1 schedules
deliverable: a cross-entity reconciliation and a responsibility map for partner reporting

name: Nth Degree CPAs
summary: Nth Degree publishes tax planning and preparation, bookkeeping, payroll, controller and fractional CFO services, plus valuation and financial-roadmap offerings.
fit: Entrepreneurs evaluating a more deliberate financial strategy relationship
scenario: An owner is considering hiring a controller and eventually selling the business. There is no immediate transaction, but tax decisions and management reporting are becoming more complicated. The owner needs a phased scope instead of buying every possible service at once.
decision: Compare phased proposals rather than broad promises of financial improvement. A narrowly scoped planning engagement can be the first step when the next decision is clear; a recurring finance team may fit when reporting gaps affect management every month.
question: Which decisions should I implement first and why?
note: A roadmap needs decision dates and measurable outputs to be useful. Distinguish tax work required now from controller support and valuation projects that may belong in a later phase.
documents: Current close process and reporting gaps; Owner goals and target decision dates; Historical financials and ownership records
deliverable: a phased service roadmap with approval points and separately priced work

name: TL;DR Accounting
summary: TL;DR Accounting markets remote accounting, reporting, tax preparation and financial coaching with a focus on therapy practices.
fit: Practice owners seeking plain-language financial and tax guidance
scenario: A therapist has opened a practice and uses personal funds for early expenses. The immediate job is separating business records and establishing an understandable close and filing process before the owner considers hiring or adding another activity.
decision: Compare a therapist-focused accounting service with a targeted setup and tax-preparation engagement. An established practice with outside investments may instead need coordinated owner planning while preserving the practice bookkeeping process.
question: What will I understand and be able to act on after each review?
note: Early bookkeeping choices can make later review harder. Ask the provider to document owner-funded expenses and explain which information must be retained so a future advisor can understand opening balances.
documents: Startup receipts and owner funding history; Business accounts and practice revenue records; Formation documents and prior personal returns
deliverable: an opening-record package and a first-year close and filing calendar

name: Graphite Financial
summary: Graphite Financial lists federal and state tax compliance, real-time advisory, R&D credits, multi-state support, entity structure planning, and year-round tax guidance. Its company overview describes integrated accounting, controllership, forecasting, tax, payroll, and financial operations for growing and venture-backed companies.
fit: Growing or venture-backed companies comparing tax services as part of an outsourced finance function.
scenario: Your high-growth company needs federal and state compliance while founders face personal liquidity decisions.
decision: A company preparing for a funding round may prioritize financial reporting, forecasts, and multi-state compliance. A profitable founder with rentals may also need personal planning that crosses company boundaries. Ask whether the quote covers the founder's returns and investments, or only the operating company.
question: Is the objective investor-ready finance infrastructure, the owner's tax plan, or both?

name: Tax Strategists of America
summary: Tax Strategists of America describes gathering client data, implementing custom strategies, preparing supporting documentation, and providing a year-end summary for the client's accountant. Its official materials identify founder Carlotta Thompson as a former IRS agent.
fit: Business owners seeking strategy implementation while potentially retaining their existing return preparer.
scenario: You want written recommendations that make implementation responsibilities clear from the start.
decision: The public services page describes an accountant handoff, so compare that workflow with a scope that includes preparation. Keeping an existing preparer can work well if responsibilities are clear. Ask for the supporting records, reconciliation process, and person responsible for resolving any difference between the plan and the filed return.
question: Who incorporates the implemented strategies into the return, and how is the preparer's review documented?

name: Pronto Advisors
summary: Pronto Advisors markets tax advisory, accounting and bookkeeping, payroll, and business formation for real estate investors, business owners, and entrepreneurs. It says it can work alongside an existing team or take over the broader relationship.
fit: Business owners and investors seeking tax strategy connected to routine accounting and payroll.
scenario: Your construction company and investment entities create intercompany transactions and different reporting needs.
decision: A full accounting transition can be useful when financial data is unreliable, but a business with a functioning team may prefer a planning project. Compare the handoff process, responsibility for payroll and filings, and how the advisory work uses monthly records. Specify who retains historical files.
question: Can the proposed tax advisory scope work with the current bookkeeper and preparer, or does it require a full transfer?

name: Proactive Tax Advisors
summary: Proactive Tax Advisors markets strategic planning for high-income service-based business owners and real estate investors. Its process includes an assessment, personalized tax strategy plan, implementation support at a chosen level, and optional ongoing optimization.
fit: Service-business owners and investors seeking a planning project with a choice of implementation support.
scenario: Your business is growing and you want to discuss a purchase or compensation change before committing to it.
decision: Compare a plan-only scope with a coordinated implementation scope before deciding which price is lower. An owner who lacks time or a reliable preparer may need more execution support. Ask which future reviews are optional and how changes in income or ownership are handled after the initial project.
question: Which implementation level is quoted, and who completes each action if the client chooses self-guided support?

name: Bracket Tax Co.
summary: Bracket Tax Co. describes a CPA practice based in Asheville serving business owners and equity-compensated professionals nationwide. Its public positioning emphasizes proactive tax planning and a year-round advisory relationship, including equity compensation and ISO planning.
fit: Business owners or equity-compensated professionals seeking year-round CPA planning.
scenario: Your business income and investment or equity events require a coordinated planning conversation.
decision: Bracket Tax Co. is distinct from Bracket Partners, the real estate incentive consulting firm. Match the correct provider to the decision. An owner with incentive stock options should compare scenario modeling and timing support; an owner primarily seeking rental depreciation should confirm that work in the proposed scope.
question: Does the proposed plan coordinate equity exercise decisions with business income and other investment activity?

name: Pillar Advisors
summary: Pillar Advisors lists bookkeeping and reporting, tax compliance and advisory, financial controls, strategic finance, and capital structure advisory. Its website says it employs CPAs and tax experts while stating that Pillar Advisors is not a public accounting firm.
fit: Growing businesses seeking an integrated accounting and financial advisory partner that also provides tax support.
scenario: You need business reporting and tax advice but want to keep your existing investment relationship.
decision: Pillar's business finance scope is relevant when an owner needs books, controls, and forward-looking financial analysis as well as tax advice. Do not infer that every service is performed under a public accounting firm engagement. Request the tax signer's identity, contracting entity, and any assurance-service limitations.
question: Who contracts for and signs the tax work, and which monthly accounting or finance services are required?

name: CSSI
summary: Its public materials describe cost segregation and specialty property-tax services.
fit: Property owners seeking a specialist for the study portion of a tax project
scenario: You have a candidate property and a CPA, but need to clarify who prepares the study and who implements the tax reporting.
decision: Ask for the study methodology, required property records, and the precise handoff to your CPA.
question: What deliverables will my return preparer receive?

name: Capstan Tax Strategies
summary: Its public materials describe cost segregation, energy-related incentives, and other specialty tax services.
fit: Owners comparing technical property studies and related incentive opportunities
scenario: Your building project could involve more than depreciation, so the service proposal needs to distinguish each technical analysis.
decision: Ask which specialty services are included and how results are coordinated with your broader tax plan.
question: Which analyses are separate from the cost segregation study?

name: Cost Seg Smart
summary: Its public materials describe online cost segregation reports marketed to rental-property owners.
fit: Owners considering a digital study workflow
scenario: You want a convenient report but need to understand the inputs, review process, and reporting support before purchase.
decision: Ask how unusual property features, renovations, and incomplete records are handled.
question: Who reviews the property facts behind the generated report?

name: Engineered Tax Services
summary: Its public materials describe cost segregation and specialty tax services, including energy and research-related incentives.
fit: Owners and businesses comparing multiple specialty tax projects
scenario: You have a property study need and another potential incentive, but they may require different evidence and engagements.
decision: Ask how each specialty project is scoped and which professional coordinates it with your tax return.
question: Which project needs to be completed first to meet my deadline?

name: KBKG
summary: Its public materials describe tax-credit and incentive consulting, including cost segregation.
fit: Businesses and property owners seeking technical specialty tax support
scenario: You want to compare a specialty-tax engagement with a household or business-wide planning engagement.
decision: Ask what technical deliverables the quote includes and whether broader planning is separately available.
question: Where does the specialty engagement end and broader tax planning begin?

name: Madison SPECS
summary: Its public materials describe national cost segregation services with engineering and CPA involvement.
fit: Owners seeking a property-study specialist and CPA coordination
scenario: You want a feasibility review before deciding which properties deserve a full study.
decision: Ask how the preliminary estimate differs from the final report and what your CPA needs for implementation.
question: What information can change the preliminary benefit estimate?

name: RE Cost Seg
summary: Its public materials describe cost segregation studies and a digital property-information workflow.
fit: Rental owners comparing specialist study services
scenario: You want to understand how a remote information-gathering process handles property-specific details.
decision: Ask how photographs, plans, renovation invoices, and unusual assets are evaluated.
question: Which records are needed beyond square footage and purchase price?

name: Cherry Bekaert
summary: Its public materials describe tax and advisory services across industries and specialized business needs.
fit: Businesses seeking a broad accounting and advisory relationship
scenario: Your company needs both owner tax planning and specialized advisory work tied to its industry.
decision: Ask which team handles the owner's planning and whether that work has a separate scope.
question: Will the proposal include my personal planning as well as company services?

name: Deloitte Tax
summary: Its public materials describe business tax, international tax, private-client, and other specialized tax services.
fit: Organizations and private clients needing broad technical capabilities
scenario: You are comparing a specialist planning engagement with a broader tax relationship involving several technical teams.
decision: Ask which actual team will deliver the owner-level work and how the engagement coordinates specialists.
question: What work is handled by the core team versus separate specialists?

name: KPMG
summary: Its public materials describe tax services across business, private-enterprise, state, international, and transaction needs.
fit: Businesses evaluating a large-firm tax relationship
scenario: Your company has a transaction or multijurisdictional issue alongside personal planning needs.
decision: Ask whether the owner-level project can be scoped separately and which specialist services are required.
question: Can the proposal distinguish the transaction project from recurring compliance?

name: Advise RE
summary: Advise RE markets year-round tax advisory and CPA services for real estate investors and developers. Its site connects planning and preparation with depreciation, 1031 exchanges, and entity structure, and also lists construction and buyer advisory services.
fit: Property owners and developers seeking a real estate-focused planning and preparation relationship.
scenario: You are operating a property business while managing personally held rentals and a potential sale.
decision: A development project can require construction and transaction advice that differs from annual rental tax preparation. Compare when each team enters the process, what records it reviews before closing, and how property decisions connect with the owner's other business income.
question: Does the engagement cover the investment purchase or development decision before closing, as well as the subsequent returns?

name: 1099 Tax Doctor
summary: Its public materials describe tax planning resources and services for independent medical professionals.
fit: 1099 physicians evaluating their business and personal tax position
scenario: You are moving from employee work to independent contracting and need an organized review of the new responsibilities.
decision: Ask how entity, payroll, retirement, and quarterly-payment decisions are sequenced.
question: What should be decided before the first year of contracting ends?
note: For a physician with both employment and independent-contracting income, build the proposal around the business actually generating the 1099 receipts. Request a separate line for the physician's individual return, any medical entity, payroll, and retirement-plan coordination. The service menu describes physician-specific tiers; a tier name should not substitute for checking which income streams and entities are accepted. AE's planning project should be compared with the same physician facts, rather than with a preparation-only price.

name: Aprio
summary: Its public materials describe tax and broader business advisory services.
fit: Businesses seeking a wider accounting and advisory relationship
scenario: Your business needs specialized services while your household needs a clearly defined tax-planning project.
decision: Ask which services are provided by the assigned team and what personal planning deliverables are included.
question: Who is responsible for connecting business advice to my household return?

name: BASIS Cost Segregation
summary: Its public materials describe a technology-supported residential cost segregation workflow.
fit: Residential investors evaluating an app-based study process
scenario: You want to compare a residential study workflow with a full review of your ability to use the resulting deductions.
decision: Ask which property types the product supports and who evaluates reporting and owner-level eligibility.
question: Does the service include analysis of my ability to use the deduction?
note: BASIS describes an online residential study workflow with professional review and a report for the buyer's CPA. Map the process from property questionnaire to supporting uploads to the final reviewed deliverable. Ask what happens when the intake reveals renovations or missing acquisition records. AE is a separate candidate for owner-level planning and implementation; a residential report purchase need not replace a trusted preparer. Compare the study product and the advisory project as separate purchases.

name: Beach Life CPA
summary: Its public materials describe nationwide accounting and tax services, including support for high-income professionals.
fit: Professionals and owners considering a remote tax relationship
scenario: Your compensation includes equity and you also have side-business or property income.
decision: Ask which equity events, state issues, and business activities are included in the planning scope.
question: Will the analysis connect equity compensation with my other income?
note: Beach Life's nationwide page describes remote tax, bookkeeping, equity-compensation, and advisory work. A household with both a business and RSUs should specify whether the quote covers recurring reconciliations or a one-time equity event. Location alone is a poor selection criterion for virtual service. Ask the assigned professional to identify the states and entities covered. An AE planning engagement should be evaluated against the same transaction deadline and household records, with operational accounting priced separately.

name: Bracket Partners
summary: Its public materials describe tax planning and advisory services.
fit: Owners comparing a planning-focused advisory relationship
scenario: You want a tax plan that can be used by the professionals already supporting your business.
decision: Ask what written deliverables are supplied and how coordination with existing advisers works.
question: Can the plan be implemented with my current CPA and bookkeeper?
note: Bracket Partners is a tax-credit, incentive, and real estate development adviser. It is distinct from Bracket Tax Co. A developer seeking credit structuring or project capitalization may need Bracket Partners' specialty work alongside a separate owner-level tax adviser. Build two scopes: the development transaction and the owners' wider planning. Do not infer that AE's standard advisory engagement substitutes for sourcing, underwriting, financing, or closing a tax-credit transaction. Coordination between the two projects can matter more than selecting one firm for everything.

name: Bright Hill Advisors
summary: Its public materials describe tax and advisory support for owners, professionals, and real estate investors.
fit: Clients seeking planning across an operating business and investments
scenario: You operate a service business and are buying investment property in a separate entity.
decision: Ask whether the engagement evaluates both activities and the household-level effect.
question: Will the business and rental recommendations use the same income forecast?
note: Bright Hill's public materials focus on real estate investors and service businesses, and describe accounting and CFO support alongside tax strategy. Compare the service company's operating records with the separately owned property's records before requesting a joint forecast. Ask whether the same professional reviews compensation, acquisitions, and cash requirements. AE's focused planning proposal may fit a defined decision while another team continues the books. Both offers need an explicit schedule for updating recommendations when business results change.

name: CPA-ROD
summary: Its public materials describe business and real estate tax planning and preparation.
fit: Owners and property investors seeking an integrated tax relationship
scenario: You need a business return and personal return to reflect the same planning assumptions.
decision: Ask how the proposal coordinates entity filings, depreciation schedules, and personal estimates.
question: Who checks that all returns reflect the agreed plan?
note: CPA-ROD describes an ongoing advisory relationship for owners and investors, including business, property, and personal-tax coordination. Decide whether the immediate need is continuing access or a bounded review before a transaction. Ask for the recurring meeting calendar, escalation route, and tasks assigned to the client. A comparison with AE should use the same planning horizon, rather than equating a year-round relationship with a one-time engagement. Request separately identified filing and accounting commitments from either proposal.

name: Compass CPA
summary: Its public materials describe real estate accounting, advisory, and related tax services.
fit: Developers, syndicators, and property businesses needing finance support
scenario: Your property entities need accounting discipline while you need owner-level planning on distributions and investments.
decision: Ask how entity reporting, investor information, and personal planning are separated and connected.
question: What records are ready before the investor-level planning review?
note: Compass CPA's real estate page addresses investors, developers, syndicators, and property managers. Those roles can need very different work: partnership reporting, acquisition advice, recurring books, or exit coordination. Describe your role and list each entity before comparing engagements. A sponsor should explicitly request investor-reporting responsibilities, while an individual landlord can ask for a focused owner review. Compare AE on the narrower deliverable it actually proposes; neither firm's broad service menu proves every transaction task is included.

name: Cost Seg Atlas
summary: Its public materials describe educational cost segregation analyses and optional technical-review services.
fit: Owners exploring a preliminary analysis before purchasing a formal study
scenario: You are evaluating a tool that expressly distinguishes an educational analysis from a signed technical study.
decision: Ask what document you receive, what review upgrades are available, and whether your CPA will accept the deliverable.
question: Am I buying an educational analysis or an implementation-ready study?
note: Cost Seg Atlas distinguishes downloadable output from an optional licensed review and describes a completeness threshold for that review. Ask which version you are purchasing and what additional work resolves incomplete evidence. A professional signature does not itself establish that an owner can use a projected deduction. Before choosing a product, have the filing professional review the input records and reporting requirements. Compare AE's separately scoped study and advisory services with the complete workflow, including any review upgrade.

name: Cost Segregation Authority
summary: Its public materials describe cost segregation and related specialty property-tax services.
fit: Owners comparing a property-focused specialty tax provider
scenario: You want a study but also need to understand what related services the proposal actually includes.
decision: Ask which property-tax projects, reporting tasks, and support terms are expressly included.
question: Does the quote include any work beyond the property study?

name: Cost Segregation Guys
summary: Its public materials describe cost segregation and related services, including Form 3115 and energy-related work.
fit: Property owners seeking a specialist for studies and associated technical tasks
scenario: Your property was acquired in an earlier year and the implementation question may differ from a current acquisition.
decision: Ask how older-property studies and any accounting-method work are coordinated with the return preparer.
question: Who is responsible for determining and preparing the reporting method?
note: Cost Segregation Guys describes virtual or in-person study options and a report with a fixed-asset schedule for the client’s CPA. Its resource menu also includes Form 3115 information. Ask which reporting tasks are actually contracted, instead of treating a resource link as either proof of inclusion or proof of exclusion. For a property owner retaining a preparer, make report acceptance and correction support explicit. Compare AE on the separately scoped owner analysis and implementation; the engineering project and wider tax engagement need different deliverables.

name: CostSeg Express
summary: Its public materials describe a fast digital cost segregation workflow marketed to rental owners.
fit: Short-term rental owners prioritizing study delivery speed
scenario: You want a quick report but have not yet established how rental-activity rules affect your tax position.
decision: Ask how the report is reviewed and arrange a separate facts-based eligibility analysis before relying on projected savings.
question: Who evaluates participation and deduction usability before I rely on the estimate?
note: CostSeg Express describes an instant PDF and identifies its studies as planning documents. For a pre-closing estimate, keep projected numbers separate from the final settlement and service-date evidence. Ask who corrects the report after closing and whether the filing professional will accept the finished deliverable. AE's role can be evaluating the wider acquisition and reporting position. A fast output is useful only if the eventual tax-return records are supported; neither delivery speed nor a marketing guarantee establishes the buyer's final result.

name: CostSegEZ
summary: Its public materials describe an online cost segregation reporting workflow.
fit: Investors considering a streamlined digital report process
scenario: You are comparing convenient online delivery with the amount of property documentation your situation requires.
decision: Ask what review occurs when renovation costs or property details do not fit standard inputs.
question: How are unusual property features and renovations reviewed?
note: CostSegEZ describes instant generation with a review option. Specify whether you want preliminary information, a final report, or a reviewed report accepted by your preparer. Compare those deliverables individually before comparing price. An owner with several properties should check whether review and corrections apply to every address or only the selected order. Ask AE for a property-by-property scope if the desired work includes both study coordination and owner-level planning. Avoid interpreting automated delivery as a statement about return preparation.

name: CostSegRx
summary: Its public materials describe cost segregation studies with a published FAQ addressing scope and required inputs.
fit: Owners who want to understand study requirements before ordering
scenario: Your land allocation and existing depreciation records need attention before a study can be implemented.
decision: Ask which basis inputs you must supply and which analyses are outside the study's stated scope.
question: Who is responsible for reviewing the land allocation?
note: CostSegRx's public material lists study work with CPA-ready deliverables and reporting support. Support language should be translated into a named task: explaining a report, preparing a calculation, or preparing and filing a form are different responsibilities. Request a handoff meeting with the existing preparer and reconcile the report to the owner's basis records. AE can be compared on the wider plan and separately priced implementation. Keep engineering documentation and owner-level analysis visible as two related workstreams.

name: CostSegregation.com
summary: Its public materials describe self-guided cost segregation software for eligible property projects.
fit: Owners considering a software-led approach to organizing a study
scenario: You have a straightforward property but want your CPA to evaluate whether the software output suits the project.
decision: Ask about supported property types, input requirements, professional review, and CPA handoff.
question: Will my CPA review the proposed output before I purchase?
note: CostSegregation.com describes self-guided software, a CPA invitation workflow, and a building-basis limit for its standard product. Check the current threshold on the official site; larger properties are directed to professional-service quoting. The important comparison is whether your property fits the software workflow and who approves the inputs. AE's advisory proposal should address the owner facts and reporting responsibilities separately from the software purchase. Inviting a CPA into a platform does not establish that filing is included in its price.

name: Crescent CPA Advisors
summary: Its public materials describe tax and accounting advisory for business owners and real estate investors.
fit: Owners seeking a coordinated business and household tax relationship
scenario: Your business and rental activity are profitable, but current projections do not show their combined effect.
decision: Ask how often forecasts are refreshed and what the engagement includes for each entity.
question: Will the planning model incorporate both business profit and rental results?
note: Crescent's accounting and advisory relationship should be evaluated around what happens between monthly reporting and a planning decision. For an owner with changing margins, request the forecast refresh date and the financial records on which it depends. Compare that operating cadence with AE's defined project milestones. If one team keeps the books and another produces the plan, assign the responsibility for notifying both when profit, payroll, or borrowing changes. The proposal should specify who reconciles the resulting assumptions before recommendations are implemented.

name: Duffy + Duffy Cost Segregation
summary: Its public materials describe engineering-based cost segregation with property-study services across states.
fit: Commercial and residential owners comparing a technical study provider
scenario: You have construction plans and invoices and want to know how a detailed technical review would use them.
decision: Ask which site information and cost records support the study and what deliverables reach the CPA.
question: How will construction records affect the study methodology?
note: For Duffy + Duffy, compare the engineering assignment at the property level: plans, invoices, site information, and the intended report recipient. A new-construction project with detailed cost records requires a different intake conversation from an acquired building with limited documentation. Ask which evidence will actually be reviewed and how unresolved items are communicated. AE's owner-level scope should identify the separate analysis and reporting work needed after delivery. A construction-focused study and a household planning engagement can be complementary.

name: Duncan Carter Tax Advisory
summary: Its public materials describe tax advisory for independent physicians and related professional-income situations.
fit: Physicians with self-employment income or partnership-related compensation
scenario: Your compensation includes a K-1 or independent practice income and you need to understand the reporting relationships.
decision: Ask what information must be obtained from the practice or partnership before personalized planning.
question: Which compensation records are needed to model my tax position?
note: Duncan Carter's official physician-planning page describes work for self-employed physicians. Separate W-2 employment from independent practice receipts and partnership distributions when requesting the proposal. Ask which statements must be obtained from the practice before a useful forecast can be prepared. AE should quote the same income sources and entities if it is being evaluated for the planning work.
